Aim: Check that Stage 1 reproduces separately fitted RIF–OLS regressions
Estimand: Coefficients and standard errors of ordinary RIF–OLS at each of 45 quantile levels
Methods compared: Stage 1 (pooled covariance; 1,000-block jackknife) against ordinary RIF–OLS
Performance measures: Coefficient difference (mean and root mean square); ratio of standard errors

Aim: Compare the computational cost of Stage 1 with separately fitted RIF–OLS regressions
Data-generating mechanism: Matched workloads: N = 2,000 with 1 or 256 variants, N = 400,000 with 1 or 1,000 variants
Methods compared: Ordinary RIF–OLS; Stage 1 with pooled or jackknife covariance
Performance measures: Time to fit with standard errors; whole-process time; peak memory (means of 3 repeats, 1 thread)

Aim: Check that Stage 2 recovers location, dispersion and mixture-component effects without bias and with calibrated standard errors
Data-generating mechanism: Normal phenotype with an effect on location, dispersion or both; two-component normal mixture with an effect on the lower-component location; N = 400,000; minor allele frequency 0.3; per-allele effects drawn from U(−0.1, 0.1)
Estimand: Population projection target of the generating effect onto the model's weights
Methods compared: Stage 2 by ordinary least squares with pooled or jackknife covariance
Performance measures: Bias over RMSE; mean SE over RMSE; 95% coverage; Monte Carlo intervals

Aim: Compare Stage 2 mixture estimates with direct mixture maximum likelihood
Data-generating mechanism: Two-component mixture with effects on the lower-component location drawn from U(−0.1, 0.1); N = 10,000, 50,000, 400,000; minor allele frequency 0.3
Methods compared: Stage 1 and mixture Stage 2 (pooled or jackknife covariance) against mixture maximum likelihood refitted at every variant
Performance measures: Bias; mean SE over RMSE; Monte Carlo intervals

Aim: Compare the cost of the two mixture methods
Performance measures: Time to fit; whole-process time; peak memory (3 panels per N); implied genome-wide cost

Aim: Compare pooled and 1,000-block jackknife standard errors for rare variants
Data-generating mechanism: Normal phenotype with no effect or a dispersion effect (c = 0.1); N = 10,000, 50,000, 400,000; minor allele frequency 0.05, 0.01, 0.001
Estimand: Population projection targets of location and dispersion effects
Performance measures: Bias and mean SE over the empirical s.d.; 95% coverage; Monte Carlo intervals

Aim: Compare pooled and jackknife standard errors at the separations of the empirical mixtures
Data-generating mechanism: Two-component normal mixtures (component s.d. 1) with the separations (1.81–5.89 s.d.) and upper-component proportions (0.43–0.48) of the testosterone and antibody mixtures; N = 10,000 (400,000 for the testosterone geometries only); minor allele frequency 0.3 or 0.05; no effect or an upper-component shift sized for |z| ≈ 5
Estimand: Population projection targets of membership and component locations
Methods compared: Pooled against jackknife covariance; also compared in the empirical fits
Performance measures: Pooled over jackknife SE; SE over empirical s.d.; 95% coverage with Monte Carlo SE

Aim: Compare the model and hybrid weight designs for the mixture membership parameter
Data-generating mechanism: Two-component skew-normal mixtures in 9 scenarios, from well separated (with and without misfit of the density in the gap between components) to heavily overlapping; N = 100,000, 400,000; minor allele frequency 0.3; in each replicate, variants with effects on each component location, on membership, on all three and on both locations, and 20 null variants
Estimand: Generating effects: lower-component location 0.055, upper-component location 0.04, membership 0.08
Methods compared: Model weights (every column divided by the fitted mixture density) against hybrid weights (membership column divided by the Stage 1 kernel density)
Performance measures: Mean estimate over truth; leakage into the lower-component location; 95% coverage; s.d. of z for null variants
